acceptanceNote: Accepted artifacts and recorded evaluations. Publication is not independent verification of research claims.
objective:
Objective: security review of the Morpho Midnight Adapter for the Cantina competition (ends 3 Dec 2026). Find real vulnerabilities with coded proofs. Do NOT submit anything anywhere, do NOT create accounts, do NOT contact the team. Deliver findings to the requester only.

Scope: repo morpho-org/vault-v2 at commit bbeda7b27ae80abcf070e0158cb8a31e87bb2286, directory src/adapters/midnight: MidnightAdapter.sol, MidnightAdapterFactory.sol, gates/IKRCompatibleEnterGate.sol, gates/IKRCompatibleEnterGateFactory.sol, gates/WhitelistEnterSubGate.sol, gates/WhitelistEnterSubGateFactory.sol, libraries/PackedDurationsLib.sol, ratifiers/MidnightAdapterPriceRatifierV1.sol, ratifiers/MidnightAdapterRateRatifierV1.sol, plus interfaces under interfaces/, gates/interfaces/, ratifiers/interfaces/. The adapter lets a Morpho Vault V2 allocate into Midnight fixed-rate, fixed-maturity markets (buys, sells, holds credit, withdraws repaid assets). Read the adapter README, NatSpec, Vault V2 docs, Midnight docs and whitepaper first.

Out of scope: issues already in the prior audit drafts (Cantina and TrustSec, Midnight Adapter, 2026-10-12), expected behaviour of trusted roles (curator, allocators, sentinels), accepted risks listed by the team.

Step 1 - build: clone at the commit, run the existing test suite with Foundry, confirm it passes.
Step 2 - review, one angle per agent: accounting and rounding in buy/sell/hold/withdraw; maturity and duration edge cases (PackedDurationsLib packing, overflow, zero and max values); price and rate ratifier checks (stale, manipulated or boundary inputs); gates and whitelists (bypass, wrong caller, factory misconfiguration); interaction with Vault V2 roles, caps and allocation ids; reentrancy and callback order with Midnight; loss realisation and bad debt; factory deployment (address prediction, duplicates); invariant and fuzz tests for each of these.
Step 3 - prove: every candidate needs a Foundry test (PoC) that runs against the pinned commit and shows the impact with numbers. No PoC = not a finding. Classify with Cantina's severity criteria (impact x likelihood). Check each candidate against the out-of-scope list and the prior audit reports.
Step 4 - independent check: a different agent re-runs each PoC from a clean clone and tries to refute the finding. Keep only findings that survive.

Deliverable: for each surviving finding: title, severity with reasoning, affected file and lines, description, the PoC test file, exact command and output, suggested fix. Separately, a ranked list of Low/Informational findings written to a high standard (clear, specific, with code references). Mark anything not fully verified as UNVERIFIED. If nothing survives, say so plainly and list what was covered.
